name: South Chungcheong
summary_text: South Chungcheong (Chungcheongnam-do) was swept into the same provincial fight over student human-rights protections that engulfed Seoul, but with the institutions on opposite sides: on 24 April 2024 the provincial council passed a bill to repeal the Chungcheongnam-do Student Human Rights Ordinance (in force since 10 July 2020; its Article 15 stipulates non-discrimination obligations based on gender identity and sexual orientation), and the provincial Office of Education sued to overturn it, obtaining a suspension of the repeal's execution from the Supreme Court on 30 May 2024, so the ordinance remains in effect. On 21 February 2025 the Chungcheongnam-do and Seoul offices of education filed a joint response to a communication from three UN special procedures, appearing as 'stakeholders (enforcing authorities)' in the repeal dispute still pending before the Supreme Court and opposing the rollback on constitutional and treaty grounds. The evidence is primarily resident-facing (student non-discrimination rules), carrying small weight for a traveler under the scoring rules; no traveler-facing enforcement action, arrest, or event obstruction is documented for this unit. The −0.02 deviation below the national 0.71 was set on the premise that the province's education office aligns with the repeal campaign; the source shows the opposite alignment - the elected council moved against SOGI protections while the enforcing education office defended them in court and won a suspension - so the record reads as mixed (a hostile council initiative, a protective institutional response) rather than one-directionally de-protective, and the deviation direction should be reviewed accordingly. No other province-specific incident or enforcement series was identified for this unit.

sources.claim_summary: Republic of Korea response (21 February 2025) to the Joint Communication from UN Special Procedures (ref. OL KOR 3/2024) on the student human-rights ordinances, filed by the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education and the Chungcheongnam-do Office of Education as 'stakeholders (enforcing authorities)' in the repeal dispute pending before the Supreme Court. The Chungnam section records: the provincial council passed a repeal bill on 24 April 2024 against the ordinance enacted 10 July 2020 (Article 15 covers gender identity and sexual orientation); the Office of Education challenged it before the Supreme Court on 13 May 2024 and obtained suspension of execution on 30 May 2024, so the ordinance remains in effect; it argues the repeal violates the Constitution and international human-rights treaties. The Seoul section records its 11 July 2024 petition against the council's abolition and the Supreme Court's 23 July 2024 suspension.
